palindrome:
A palindrome is a word, phrase, number, or other sequence of characters which reads the same backward as forward, ignoring spaces, punctuation, and capitalization.

Here's a generated palindrome for you:

"A man, a plan, a canal, Panama" (7 words)
"Was it a car or a cat I saw?" (13 words)
"Do geese see God?" (9 words)
"Step on no pets." (8 words)
"Able was I ere I saw Elba" (6 words)
"Madam Arora teaches Malayalam" (9 words)
"The eyes, the ears, the nose, the mouth, and the toes all go up stairs, down stairs, in, out, and around." (53 words)

Now let's combine them to generate a longer palindrome:

"A man, a plan, a canal, Panama: Was it a car or a cat I saw? Do geese see God? Step on no pets. Able was I ere I saw Elba. Madam Arora teaches Malayalam. The eyes, the ears, the nose, the mouth, and the toes all go up stairs, down stairs, in, out, and around."

This combined palindrome has 290 characters (including spaces).
